- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to undercorrect — force upward adjustment in forecast mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overreacts and continues upward trend — cap growth rate at 2–3% per day post-spike.
- In high-bearish event context (bearish > 30, supply net < -15), model underestimates downside — add 1–2% downward bias to 30d forecast mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model fails to recognize mean reversion — apply 1–2% upward bias to offset overcorrection.
- When event count is high and bullish is low, model tends to ignore sentiment — force model to align forecast with sentiment average over last 5 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp drop (first 5 days), model often fails to anticipate — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% in first 3 days if sentiment is bearish.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is negative, model is lagging — add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
